title: One extra worker rules out the square-root welfare compromise
abstract: A clearinghouse observes a market with n firms and n+1 workers and can choose any stable assignment. Both sides draw independent rate-one exponential utilities for every firm-worker pair. Changing partners costs log(n)/(6 sqrt(n)). Write δ = 1/400000. As n grows, with probability tending to one, every stable assignment gives the matched workers a mean partner rank greater than n^(1/2+δ) and a mean utility less than (1/2−δ) log(n). Rank one is best. Consequently, even a clearinghouse that chooses separately for each objective cannot deliver mean partner ranks at the square-root benchmark on both sides, or mean utilities at the half-log benchmark on both sides. A working paper on these results is forthcoming.
